name: Retail
description: A shop-floor business that trades long hours, runs shifts and has to see, at any moment, who is on the floor, who is not, and what the week is costing. This preset suggests the modules a retail deployment usually needs, the departments and job families a store is usually built from, the shift patterns that cover a trading week, the leave types a shop usually offers, and the views a store manager opens first. It decides none of the things that depend on where the business is: leave entitlement, tax, contributions, break length and the pay period all come from a verified rule pack, and the currency is a placeholder the customer confirms.

modules.description: Employee records, departments and jobs. A shop cannot roster or pay anybody without them.
Clocking in at the store and the recorded hours the roster is judged against and the pay run is calculated from.
The working-time model of a shop: the trading week, the clock-in tolerance and the breaks.
Shift templates and the roster that covers the trading week.
The leave a shop offers and the cover that has to be found for it.
The monthly pay run. It stays switched off until a verified rule pack is attached.
Shop staff are hired often, and the offer has to be produced the same way every time.
The trading and labour figures a store manager and an area manager read.
The shop floor books its own shifts, sees its own hours and asks for leave.
A shop's staff list rarely starts in the product; it arrives as a file.
How many hours the shop needs next week, once there is enough history to be worth forecasting.

workforce.description: How the workforce records are kept: the optional fields the tenant holds on a person and the way the organisation is described. The fields a shop keeps on a person, and the way its stores are described.

time_tracking.description: How the hours are recorded: A mobile clock-in at the store, with the site geofence switched on so that a clock-in only counts inside the building. The break and rest rules the law sets are not here; they come from the attached rule pack.

time.description: The working-time model: the week starts on monday, a clock-in is accepted a short time either side of the shift, and the breaks are the ones the roster shows. The length of a statutory break, the daily working-time limit and the minimum rest between two shifts come from the rule pack.

break_rules.description: The break the roster shows, for every site that has no rule of its own.

scheduling.description: The roster patterns a shop runs: an early opening shift, a full trading day, a late close and the weekend cover. The roster is published a week at a time. The working-time limit, the minimum rest between shifts and the number of days in a row that may be worked come from the rule pack.

shift_templates.name: Early
shift_templates.description: Opens the shop and covers the trade until the middle of the day.

shift_templates.name: Full Day
shift_templates.description: A whole trading day on the floor.

shift_templates.name: Late
shift_templates.description: Covers the evening trade and closes the shop.

shift_templates.name: Weekend Cover
shift_templates.description: The extra cover the weekend trade needs.

leave.description: The leave a shop offers and the approval it needs. The entitlement, the accrual rhythm, the carry-over and the right to be paid for unused leave are decided by the rule pack, not here.

leave_types.name: Annual Leave
leave_types.description: The holiday the shop's staff take.

leave_types.name: Family Leave
leave_types.description: The absence that a family matter causes.

leave_types.name: Unpaid Leave
leave_types.description: The absence the staff take and are not paid for.

payroll.description: The pay run a shop expects: monthly, with the components the jurisdiction may require. Every rate and amount is left to the rule pack, so payroll stays disabled until a verified pack is attached to the tenant.

statutory_components.label: Income tax
statutory_components.description: The tax withheld from the employee's pay. The rate comes from the rule pack; the preset only names the component so the customer can see it.

statutory_components.label: Social contributions
statutory_components.description: The employer contribution the jurisdiction requires. The rate comes from the rule pack; the preset only names the component.

statutory_leave_pay.description: Which of the leave types above the tenant expects to be paid and which it expects to be unpaid. The fraction of pay a statutory leave attracts is set by the rule pack, not here.

recruiting.description: How a shop hires: the standard offer letter, and the checks a candidate is asked to consent to. The consent scope and what a candidate must be told about the checks are set by the law of the tenant's jurisdiction, so the scope is left to the rule pack.

reporting.description: The organisation-wide figures a store manager and an area manager read, and the exports behind them.

ess.description: The screens the shop floor uses for itself: the shifts it works, the hours it has recorded and the leave it asks for.

imports.description: How the shop brings its own records in: the templates, the dry run and the confirmation before anything is written.

forecasting.description: How the shop works out the hours it will need, once there is enough history to be worth forecasting.

organisation_templates.description: The store structure a retail business is usually built from. The customer may rename, move or refuse any of it: this is a starting point for a conversation, not a decision the preset has taken.

action_queues.name: Roles still to fill

forecast_drivers.description: What a shop can forecast once it has a season of history: the hours it needs on the floor and the cover it needs when somebody is away.

drivers.name: Planned trading hours
drivers.description: The hours the shop is open, which move the labour demand with them.

drivers.name: Seasonal footfall
drivers.description: How busy the shop is through the year, which moves the hours it needs.

drivers.name: Staff availability
drivers.description: Who is available to work, which moves the cover that can be found.

required_data.name: Recorded hours
required_data.description: Enough recorded hours to see the shape of the trading week.

required_data.name: Shift patterns
required_data.description: The shifts the shop actually rosters, so the forecast has a pattern to follow.

required_data.name: Absence history
required_data.description: A history of who was away, so the forecast does not promise cover that will not exist.

import_templates.description: The shop's staff list, when it arrives as a file rather than being typed in one person at a time.

import_templates.name: Department import
import_templates.description: The store structure, when the customer already has one.

import_templates.name: Job import

import_templates.name: Leave balance import
import_templates.description: The balances carried over from the previous system.

import_templates.name: Shift template import
import_templates.description: The shift patterns the shop already runs, when they are already written down.

exclusions.name: Statutory leave entitlement and accrual
exclusions.description: How many days of leave an employee is entitled to, how the entitlement accrues, how much may be carried into the next year and whether unused leave may be paid out.
exclusions.reason: These are set by the law of the tenant's jurisdiction and differ from one country to the next. A preset has no jurisdiction, so it names the slot and leaves the number to a verified rule pack.

exclusions.name: Tax, contributions and the statutory pay components
exclusions.description: The deductions, allowances and employer contributions the jurisdiction requires, and the rates they are charged at.
exclusions.reason: A tax rate and a contribution percentage are the most tightly guarded numbers in the product. They live in a verified rule pack and nowhere else, and payroll stays disabled until one is attached to the tenant.

exclusions.name: Minimum wage and pay floors
exclusions.description: The lowest pay the tenant may offer, and the floor that applies to a grade, a contract type or a working time.
exclusions.reason: The floor is set by the jurisdiction and changes with it. The tenant's own pay structure may sit above it, but the preset may not state it.

exclusions.name: Working-time limits, break length and minimum rest
exclusions.description: The daily and weekly working-time limits, the length of a statutory break, whether the break is paid, the minimum rest between two shifts and the number of days in a row that may be worked.
exclusions.reason: Every one of these is a working-time rule of the jurisdiction. The preset leaves the slots open so that the rule pack fills them with the values that apply where the tenant actually is.

exclusions.name: Notice periods and termination
exclusions.description: The notice an employee or an employer must give, and what happens to the contract when it ends.
exclusions.reason: Notice is a jurisdiction rule, and in some places it depends on the length of service and the reason for the ending. The tenant decides what it will do, and the rule pack tells it what it must do.

exclusions.name: Background check consent and disclosure
exclusions.description: Which checks a candidate may be offered, what the candidate must be told about them and what the candidate has to consent to.
exclusions.reason: Data-protection and employment law usually set both the scope and the wording. The preset leaves the scope to the rule pack so that the tenant never offers a check it is not allowed to offer.

exclusions.name: Data protection and retention
exclusions.description: How long the tenant keeps each kind of record, which records it may keep at all, and what happens to them when a person asks for them to be erased.
exclusions.reason: The retention periods and the rights are a matter for the tenant's own policy and for the law that applies to it. The product supports the workflows; it does not decide the periods.

exclusions.name: Pay frequency and currency
exclusions.description: The preset carries a monthly pay cycle and a placeholder currency. The tenant confirms both, and the jurisdiction may restrict either.
exclusions.reason: The pay period and the currency are the tenant's own commercial choices, but the law of the jurisdiction constrains them, so the tenant has to confirm them rather than inherit them.

exclusions.name: Trading hours and the shop calendar
exclusions.description: When the shop opens, when it closes, and the days it is shut.
exclusions.reason: The preset suggests a week that starts on Monday and a roster published a week at a time. The trading hours and the holiday calendar are the shop's own, and they change with the season.
